title: Wendell and the Compass
premise: Lena Thornbury flies medicine and gossip into the interior, keeping her crew moving because every place they've stopped has cost them someone. When old rival Cass Merrow hires them for a run upriver during monsoon season, Lena discovers the cargo is tied to the smuggling operation her late brother died exposing — the one the crew swore off and the law never touched. Betrayed mid-river, stranded with a leaking boat, they survive on the help of a stranger, Ilya, who knows the water better than anyone and wants justice of his own. In the end, Lena chooses to stop running: she delivers the evidence that convicts the man the courts could never reach, accepts that belonging means staying to face what comes after, and lets the crew finally put down roots.
about_author: Tamsin Marchetti spent a decade working seasonal jobs in river towns and bush strips before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people who keep moving — and about the moment they decide not to.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rain, Rumors
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She lands at a muddy strip with medicine crates and hears the first rumor: Cass Merrow is asking around about her crew. The beat is wary routine — Lena's rule is never stay long enough to be found.

chapters.title: The Crew That Keeps Moving
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet the crew: mechanic Dez, navigator Sefa, young runner Pip. A near-miss with a debt collector in town shows why they can't stop. Beat: loyalty forged by flight.

chapters.title: An Old Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Cass arrives unannounced with a contract too good to refuse: one run upriver, triple pay, monsoon be damned. Lena refuses; Dez's hidden debts force a vote. Beat: the past knocking with money in hand.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Flashback woven through present argument: the job years ago that got Lena's brother Tomas killed, the oath the crew swore over his grave. Beat: grief as the true contract.

chapters.title: Loading the Lie
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They take the job but inspect the crates secretly — medical supplies hiding something else. Cass's manifest doesn't add up. Beat: suspicion sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Upriver Into the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The flight and river transfer go wrong fast; weather closes in and they must switch to an old boat for the last leg. Beat: commitment — no turning back now.

chapters.title: What the Crates Hold
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip pries open a crate and finds ledgers and sealed evidence — records of the smuggling ring Tomas died chasing, bound for destruction. Beat: the dead brother's unfinished work in their hands.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Blackwater Bend
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Cass's men intercept mid-river, seize the evidence, strand the crew on a leaking boat, and leave them for the monsoon. Beat: betrayal confirming every fear about stopping.

chapters.title: Taking On Water
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A desperate night bailing and patching; Pip nearly goes overboard. The crew's survival skills are all they have left. Beat: terror binding them tighter than any oath.

chapters.title: The Stranger on the Sandbar
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They limp ashore and find Ilya, a river pilot living off-grid who recognizes the boat — it belonged to a friend Cass ruined. He offers help at a price: he comes along. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Ilya's Map
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. He knows backchannels through the flooded country where Cass's men must slow down. His own loss surfaces — his partner jailed on falsified charges. Beat: two kinds of justice meeting.

chapters.title: Running the Flooded Country
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. A harrowing passage through drowned forest and rapids, patching the leak with canvas and prayer. Beat: competence under pressure, fragile hope.

chapters.title: The River Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They resupply in a town where everyone knows Cass and fears him; an old woman gives them Tomas's last letter, mailed before he died. Beat: the community the law forgot.

chapters.title: Tomas's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Reading the letter, Lena learns Tomas had copied the ledgers and hid the originals — proof enough to convict if they can reach it. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Hunted on the Water
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Cass's gunboat finds their trail; a chase through narrow channels ends with the boat holed worse and Dez wounded. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Where the Law Doesn't Go
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Hiding in a smugglers' cache, the crew debates: hand the evidence to corrupt officials and lose it, or use it themselves. Beat: choosing justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Hidden Originals
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following Tomas's clues, they recover the ledger originals from a drowned chapel. Cass's men close in. Beat: the brother's voice guiding them home.

chapters.title: Storm Front
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The monsoon's worst hits as they make their final run toward the regional magistrate's station — and Cass waits there ahead of them. Beat: everything converging.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Landing
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax: Lena faces Cass directly, trading the truth of what he did to Tomas and Ilya's partner against his threats. Ilya's river knowledge turns his ambush. Beat: courage over fear.

chapters.title: Delivering the Dead Man's Evidence
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. With the storm breaking, they get the ledgers to the magistrate and witnesses come forward from the river towns. Cass is taken into custody. Beat: justice arriving, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Cost Tally
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Aftermath: Dez healing, the boat beyond repair, debts settled at last. Each character reckons what the run cost them. Beat: mourning and relief entwined.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Resolution: instead of flying out, Lena signs a lease on a riverside strip — a base, a home. The crew stays; Ilya stays. Beat: belonging chosen at last, the moving finally over.
